channel.description: Latest articles from Otago Daily Times (odt.co.nz)

item.title: Patron locked in pub after falling asleep
item.description: It's believed the man fell asleep in a toilet at the Waterloo Hotel. PHOTO: GREGOR RICHARDSON A man was forced to mount an escape attempt from a Dunedin pub after he woke in a toilet after-hours to find himself locked in.

item.title: Stellar day at Laneway
item.description: Laneway Festival 2026Western Springs, Auckland Friday, February 5 REVIEWED BY DEBBIE PORTEOUS Most surely went away from Laneway 2026 having life affirmed after a lightly fruity, fizzing day in the sun with their pals.

item.title: Kiwi snowboarders off to flying start
item.description: New Zealand has made a flying start to the Winter Olympics in Italy, with all three men qualifying for the final of the snowboard Big Air event.

item.title: Driver took out motorway barrier before fleeing: police
item.description: Photo: ODT files A driver took out a 100m section of median barrier on Dunedin's Southern Motorway before absconding from the early-morning crash, police say.

item.title: Wastewater discharged into Cook Strait again
item.description: Sewage can be seen on Wellington's south coast after a leak from the Moa Point wastewater plant. Photo: Kate Taptiklis Wellington Water says screened wastewater is now being discharged straight into the Cook Strait again after days of it being near the shoreline on the city's south coast.

item.title: Kidnapped mother of TV host presumed still alive
item.description: A notice requests information on the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie. Photo: Pima County Sheriff’s Office via Reuters Investigators presume the kidnapped elderly mother of popular US TV news host Savannah Guthrie is "still out there" and alive four days after she was abducted from her Arizona home, though no suspect has been identified, authorities say.

item.title: Britain's PM apologises to Epstein victims
item.description: British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has launched a fierce attack on his former United States ambassador Peter Mandelson, seeking to assuage anger from across British politics and saying he was sorry he had believed his "lies" before appointing him.

item.title: Aboriginal group shows support at Waitangi
item.description: An Aboriginal group say being present at Waitangi is about strengthening ties between Indigenous nations. Photo: RNZ By Layla Bailey-McDowell of RNZ A group of Aboriginal manuhiri (visitors) say they have travelled across the Tasman to stand alongside Māori at Waitangi, drawing on shared experiences as Indigenous peoples navigating the impacts of government policy on culture, language and land.

item.title: Mosgiel chemical spill contained
item.description: A hazmat unit responded to a chemical spill in Mosgiel today.

item.title: Holland injury taints Highlanders win
item.description: Fabian Holland leaves the field with a shoulder injury during their preseason game against Moana Pasifika in Queenstown this afternoon. Photo: Tracey Roxburgh The Highlanders' 41-31 preseason win against Moana Pasifika has been overshadowed by what appears to be a serious injury to star lock Fabian Holland.
